accuracy.evidence: Problem types and unknown positions follow the CCSS Mathematics Table 1 of common addition and subtraction situations (add to, take from, put together/take apart, compare; result, change and start unknown) behind 1.OA.1, and the NC Year 1 statement including the 7 = □ − 9 missing number example. Every story was solved by hand and checked back: 7 + 5 = 12, 6 + 9 = 15, 3 + 8 = 11, 12 − 7 = 5, 15 − 9 = 6, 13 − 6 = 7, 8 + 5 = 13, 14 − 6 = 8, 9 + 4 = 13, 13 − 9 = 4, 15 − 8 = 7, 17 − 11 = 6, 16 − 9 = 7, 12 − 4 = 8. All numbers stay within 20. The adult text says change and start unknown are harder, as in Carpenter and colleagues' Cognitively Guided Instruction research, without claiming a fixed order for every child.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips documented for early word problems (keyword reliance, giving a given number as the answer, the bigger number for compare, the equals sign read as 'the answer comes next', no check): 'more means add' in the step 2 prediction, the 19 option after counting on and challenge 'more'; 'away means take away' in the step 3 prediction and wrong sentence cards; the whole given back as the answer (12 option, challenge 'whole'); answering compare with the bigger number (step 4 feedback, p4, m5, challenge 'compare'); 7 = □ − 9 in step 5, m3 and challenge 'equals'; answers that cannot fit (16 left from 12, 3 ducks at first, 25 grapes).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagwprob is built on the part–whole bar model for numbers to 20 with the unknown moved around: placing whole and parts, counting on to a missing part along 20 cubes, choosing the inverse sentence for a missing start, marking unpartnered cubes for a difference, and judging answers. flagstory acts out add-to and take-from within 10 with the objects themselves and has no bar model, no change or start unknown and no compare; flagaddtog, flagtake and flagpme cover combining, taking away and the part–whole cherry diagram. lab_distinct gate passes under 30%.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child finds the structure by doing it: a part dropped on the whole bar is sent back as 'only a part', counting on lights orange cubes from 7 to 12 and an overshoot turns red, the 19 and 12 answer buttons explain why they are wrong, picking 8 − 5 for the birds says 3 birds could not lose 5, tapping a partnered cube says it has a partner, and 16 left from 12 sweets is shown to be impossible. The text after each task only names what the child just did.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options the lab disproves: '9, the apples left' as the whole (the bar sends 9 to a part), 'Yes, more means add' for the shells (counting on gives 5, and 19 is rejected), and 'Yes, away means take away' for the birds (8 − 5 = 3 is rejected because 5 cannot fly away from 3).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge questions covering change unknown, start unknown, compare more, compare fewer, 7 = □ − 9 and a sense check; every wrong option carries one of six distinct messages: added the whole on, gave a number from the story, took away instead of adding back, gave one amount instead of the difference, misread the equals sign, and an answer bigger than the start after eating some.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs are short sentences built round one worked story each and pass the family kid readability limit; the adult text names CCSS 1.OA.1, the NC Year 1 wording and the terms part, whole, part–whole model, bar model, count on, difference, number sentence and inverse. Canvas text is one short story at a time in a large box, and the young layout gives big buttons.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate clean. Each kid paragraph handles one problem shape (whole and parts, missing part, missing start, compare and checking). Items span change unknown (p1, m1, m4), start unknown (p2, m2, m6), the whole (p3, m7), compare (p4, m5), sense checks (p5, m8), the equals sign (m3) and keyword thinking (m9), with numbers varied by parameters.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px Android light, 360 px dark, and desktop light and dark screenshots of every step before and after Show me. At 360 px the story box wraps to three lines, the bar model and three 86 px number cards fit, the 20 counting cubes sit in two rows of 10 at about 33 px, the compare trains are laid out in interleaved rows of 10 so partners sit one above the other, and the two judge buttons are 78 px tall. Drags onto the bar and along the cubes were tested with the mouse.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: put each number on the whole or a part, add or take off a cube, pick the missing part, choose either number sentence, mark any cube near the end of the longer train (including a partnered one, so the slip is possible by button too), and Makes sense or Not right. The canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action with the reason. walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in light and dark themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
